theme: Product-launch monitors: certificate transparency (crt.sh) tooling, app release-notes scrapers, Wayback diff tools, help-center change monitors, trademark/patent (USPTO, PatentsView) clients
queries_run: crt.sh python client github certificate transparency (blocked - web search budget exhausted mid-run)
wayback machine diff tool github python archived pages (blocked - web search budget exhausted mid-run)
patentsview api python client github (blocked - web search budget exhausted mid-run)
uspto trademark api python client github (blocked - web search budget exhausted mid-run)

candidates.name: web-monitoring (EDGI)
candidates.what_it_holds: Umbrella org/repo for the Environmental Data & Governance Initiative's web-monitoring toolkit: a PostgreSQL-backed DB (web-monitoring-db), automated crawlers/diffing service (web-monitoring-processing), and a React diff-viewer UI. Tracks page snapshots + change metadata + human annotations across thousands-to-tens-of-thousands of monitored government pages, with Internet Archive integration for point-in-time capture. 123 commits on the umbrella repo, GPLv3 code / CC-BY-SA-4.0 docs.
candidates.why_useful: This is exactly the architecture needed for gap #15/#17: a help-center or product-page change monitor with point-in-time snapshots and structured diffs. Could be repointed at Airbnb's help center, newsroom, or app-release pages to detect policy/feature changes and product launches with timestamped versions -- point-in-time by construction, which fits rule #2 discipline.
candidates.size_hint: 8 sub-repos; DB of snapshots not itself on GitHub (self-hosted)
candidates.last_activity: active as of fetch; exact date not surfaced

candidates.name: changedetection.io
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-hostable website change-detection app (~2,496 commits): watches arbitrary URLs, diffs content via CSS/XPath/JSONPath selectors, supports PDF and browser-rendered (Playwright) pages, and fires notifications (Slack/Discord/webhook) on change. No committed dataset -- it is a running service you point at target pages.
candidates.why_useful: Directly usable, no-code way to build a help-center / app-release-notes / newsroom change monitor for Airbnb (and comparators Vrbo, Booking, Vacasa) to catch product-launch and policy-change timing ahead of scraped confirmation -- fits gap #15 (product/patent/trademark & release monitors) as a generic acquisition method rather than site-specific script.
candidates.size_hint: single Python app, Docker image available

candidates.name: waybackpy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package + CLI wrapping Internet Archive's SavePageNow, CDX Server, and Availability APIs -- lets you enumerate every archived snapshot timestamp for a URL and pull specific captures. 497 commits, 604 stars, MIT.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a scriptable way to reconstruct point-in-time history of Airbnb's help center, newsroom, app-store listing page, or trademark/press pages via Wayback captures -- useful for the release-notes/help-center diff workstream and for point-in-time discipline generally (gap #4, #17).
candidates.time_coverage: however far Wayback has crawled the target URL

candidates.name: waybackpack
candidates.what_it_holds: CLI tool to bulk-download every Wayback Machine capture of a given URL into a local timestamp-organized archive, with date-range filtering. 114 commits, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Complementary bulk-download tool to waybackpy for reconstructing full historical capture sets of Airbnb help-center/app pages or competitor product pages (Vrbo, Booking) for a diff-based product-launch/policy-change timeline.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: same purpose as waybackpy above; keep both since one is bulk-download CLI, the other is API wrapper

candidates.name: certstream-python
candidates.what_it_holds: Python WebSocket client for the CertStream network, which aggregates real-time Certificate Transparency log feeds (domain names, fingerprints, issuer, timestamps). 36 commits, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Real-time feed that could flag newly issued TLS certs for new Airbnb subdomains (e.g. a new product/microsite launch, an acquisition's domain going live, or a new country TLD) ahead of press coverage -- a leading indicator method for gap #15's product-launch monitor idea. Needs to run forward from now; can't backfill history.

candidates.name: crt.sh (Python wrapper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python API wrapper (`crtshAPI().search('domain.com')`) around crt.sh's certificate-transparency search, returning certificate metadata (issuer, domain names, timestamps) for any queried domain. 20 commits, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Can backfill historical certificate-issuance history (crt.sh keeps a searchable CT log archive) for airbnb.com and subsidiary/product subdomains -- a point-in-time-flavored way to date when a new product domain first appeared, unlike the real-time-only certstream feed above.
candidates.time_coverage: however far crt.sh's CT log ingestion goes (years)

candidates.name: google-play-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Pure-Python Google Play Store client: app metadata (title, description, rating, price, developer), paginated user reviews, permissions, and search results. Does NOT expose release-notes/version history directly (Play Store API limitation). 187 commits, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Feeds gap #5 (engagement: app downloads/rankings, review sentiment) -- Airbnb app rating trends and review volume/sentiment on Google Play as an engagement proxy, refreshed on a schedule for a point-in-time series (ratings/review counts change over time, so repeated pulls with pull-dates would be usable).
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshot only per pull; needs repeated pulls for a series

candidates.name: app-store-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js client for Apple's iTunes/App Store: app metadata, reviews (sortable/paginated), rating histograms, and -- notably -- a `versionHistory` method that returns the app's release-notes/version-history log directly. 164 commits, 1.4k stars, MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers the 'app release-notes scraper' theme: `versionHistory` gives Airbnb's iOS release cadence and changelog text, which can be timestamped to flag feature launches (e.g. new product lines, RNPL rollout, regional expansion mentions) ahead of earnings commentary -- a genuinely point-in-time-able series since Apple's version-history is itself dated.
candidates.time_coverage: full version-history back to app's release history as Apple retains it

candidates.name: patent_client
candidates.what_it_holds: Archived (April 2026) Python ORM-style unified client covering USPTO Patent Examination Data, Open Data Portal, Global Dossier, Patent Assignments, PTAB, Patent Public Search, Bulk Data Storage, plus EPO Inpadoc. Pandas-integrated, Pydantic v2 models. 632 commits, 128 stars, Apache 2.0. Note: archived/read-only, successor is an AI-agent-focused rewrite not evaluated here.
candidates.why_useful: One client covers multiple USPTO patent/assignment endpoints, so it could pull Airbnb's (and Vacasa/Sonder/Booking's) patent filing and assignment history as a very-low-frequency but genuine leading indicator of product roadmap (gap #15). Being archived means it may need patching for current USPTO API changes.
candidates.time_coverage: however far USPTO bulk/API data goes

candidates.name: patentsview (R client)
candidates.what_it_holds: rOpenSci-reviewed R client for the PatentsView API (disambiguated USPTO patent database, 5.8M+ patents, coverage from ~2007). `search_pv()` supports JSON-based queries against patent, assignee, and citation fields. 556 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Could pull Airbnb's (assignee-disambiguated) patent grant history and technology-category tags over time as a slow-moving product-roadmap signal (gap #15) -- R rather than Python, but PatentsView's disambiguated assignee IDs are the main value-add over raw USPTO bulk data.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps parker­hancock/patent_client's PatentsView-adjacent coverage; keep as R alternative

candidates.name: PatentsView-Evaluation
candidates.what_it_holds: Official PatentsView repo benchmarking/evaluating the entity-disambiguation algorithms (assignee/inventor deduplication) underlying the PatentsView database. 16 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal -- documents data-quality caveats for anyone using PatentsView assignee data (e.g. how reliably 'Airbnb, Inc.' filings are deduplicated), useful context rather than a data source itself.

candidates.name: uspto-patent-citation-graph
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool that downloads patent citation data via the PatentsView API and loads it into SQL databases for network/citation-graph analysis. 16 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal for ABNB specifically (citation-network analysis is more an R&D-intensity tool for hardware/tech firms); listed for completeness under the patent-client theme.
candidates.time_coverage: however far PatentsView citation data goes

candidates.name: certspotter
candidates.what_it_holds: Go-based lightweight Certificate Transparency log monitor (1.2k stars) that watches CT logs and alerts on new certificates for configured domains.
candidates.why_useful: Same product-launch-detection use case as certstream-python/crt.sh above (new Airbnb subdomain = new product/microsite), implemented as a standalone monitoring daemon rather than a library -- an alternative if a always-on watcher is preferred over a Python script.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps CaliDog/certstream-python and PaulSec/crt.sh for the same use case

candidates.name: sublert
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool that leverages Certificate Transparency logs to automatically monitor and alert on newly deployed subdomains for a target organization. 1k stars.
candidates.why_useful: Purpose-built for exactly this theme's 'product-launch monitor via CT' idea -- point it at airbnb.com (and Vrbo/Vacasa/Sonder) to catch new subdomains signaling product or market launches before press coverage.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps certstream-python/crt.sh/certspotter for the CT-monitoring use case; this one is purpose-built for org-level subdomain monitoring specifically

candidates.name: ctfr
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool for enumerating HTTPS subdomains of a target by querying Certificate Transparency logs (crt.sh backend). 2.1k stars.
candidates.why_useful: One more implementation of the same CT-log subdomain-enumeration idea; lower marginal value once crt.sh wrapper + sublert + certspotter are already catalogued, but very popular/well-maintained so worth a line.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicates the CT-monitoring capability of PaulSec/crt.sh, sublert, certspotter

notes: Web search (WebSearch tool) hit the session-wide 200-query budget cap on the very first 4 queries of this run (shared across all parallel scouts in this sweep) -- every subsequent query in the notes/queries_run list above was done via WebFetch against known GitHub repo URLs, github.com/topics/<tag> tag pages, and one github.com/search page (which then hit a 429 rate limit after two uses and had to be abandoned). This means the sweep for this theme is narrower than a full web-search pass would have been: I relied on prior knowledge of well-known repos in each sub-area (crt.sh/CT tooling, Wayback tooling, app-store scrapers, PatentsView/USPTO clients, EDGI web-monitoring) and verified each by fetching its GitHub page directly, rather than discovering candidates fresh via search. No Kaggle/Zenodo/Dataverse/HuggingFace pages or awesome-lists were reachable given the search outage -- worth a follow-up scout once search budget resets. All 15 candidates are acquisition-method/tooling repos (data_kind='acquisition_method'); none had a committed historical Airbnb-specific dataset, which is expected for this theme (these are generic clients/monitors, not Airbnb-specific archives). The two highest-value finds are edgi-govdata-archiving/web-monitoring (a full point-in-time change-detection architecture, adaptable to Airbnb's help center/newsroom) and facundoolano/app-store-scraper (has a genuine versionHistory/release-notes endpoint, which is the literal ask of this theme). CT-log tooling (crt.sh, certstream, sublert, certspotter, ctfr) is real but only forward-looking or shallow-historical for a domain-launch signal, and is a stretch as an ABNB KPI input -- flagged low/medium accordingly. Recommend a follow-up scout with `gh search` (once other agents free up that budget) specifically for 'site:github.com airbnb app release notes dataset' and 'USPTO trademark bulk data TSDR csv' which this run could not reach.
